notes: Last night's result: only 9 merchants are formally 'churned', and they are all tiny (1-11 orders in their final quarter, many with zero prior-period history) - these look like accounts that never gained traction rather than established businesses declining, so there isn't much of a "warning sign" trend to extract from them, and ticket/refund signals are mostly flat at zero. To give the task force something more useful, tonight I broaden the net to substantial merchants who have gone quiet without being flagged 'churned' (silent churn), and start on the shopper-level asks from Chloe and Daniel: does marketing disengagement or worse support precede a shopper going quiet. These are both new, independent questions at a different grain, so each gets its own report.

requests.title: Silent-churn merchants: substantial accounts gone quiet without a churned flag
requests.question: Beyond the 9 formally churned merchants, which substantial merchants have gone quiet without yet being flagged as churned?
requests.grain: one row per merchant (tenant), status not churned, no orders in 180+ days, lifetime orders at least 20
requests.details: Tenants with status not equal to churned. From orders (excluding cancelled): last order date is max placed_at; include only tenants whose last order date is before 2025-07-09 (180+ days before 2026-01-05) and whose lifetime order count is at least 20. lifetime revenue EUR is sum of grand_total converted to EUR via exchange_rates matched to placed_at. days since last order is 2026-01-05 minus last order date. Order by lifetime revenue EUR descending, tie-break tenant_id. Cap 50 rows, note total count.
builds_on: Pre-churn warning signs across sales, repeat buying, refunds, and support tickets

requests.title: Marketing engagement before shoppers go quiet: lapsed vs active shoppers
requests.question: Do shoppers who stop engaging with campaigns go quiet sooner, and does disengagement show up before they lapse?
requests.grain: one row per shopper group and time window before reference date
requests.details: Two groups, each needing at least 3 lifetime orders excluding cancelled: 'lapsed' = last order placed_at 180 to 365 days before 2025-12-31; 'active' = last order within 90 days of 2025-12-31. Reference date is the user's own last order date for lapsed, and 2025-12-31 for active. Two windows per group: '0-90 days before reference' and '91-180 days before reference'. From campaign_messages (sent_at, opened_at, clicked_at) count sent, opened, clicked per group/window; open rate pct is opened divided by sent; click rate pct is clicked divided by sent; shopper count is distinct users in that window. Order by shopper group, then window ascending. Expect 4 rows.

requests.title: Support experience before shoppers go quiet: lapsed vs active shoppers
requests.question: Do shoppers who get slower or worse support go quiet sooner, and does that show up before they lapse?
requests.grain: one row per shopper group and time window before reference date
requests.details: Same two groups and windows as the marketing-engagement report: 'lapsed' (last order 180-365 days before 2025-12-31) vs 'active' (last order within 90 days), reference date is last order date for lapsed and 2025-12-31 for active, windows '0-90 days before reference' and '91-180 days before reference'. From tickets (created_at, first_response_at, requester_user_id) count tickets and avg first response hours per group/window; from csat_responses (submitted_at, score, respondent_user_id) avg score per group/window. Order by shopper group, then window ascending. Expect 4 rows.
